comments.body: hmm, very weird that it doesn't work with this setup, maybe we have opposite problems in InstantSearch as in Angular InstantSearch. Does someone have a hunch?

hey @Haroenv can you provide the codesample that demonstrates the issue with `import EventEmitter from 'events';`?
I don't think I've ever encountered it.
I'll close this for now, then see if it comes back. Seems like both options aren't ideal.

I'm getting this now and the solution looks to be the same one proposed here.

```
ERROR in .../node_modules/instantsearch.js/es/lib/InstantSearch.d.ts(94,97):
94:97 Type 'typeof EventEmitter' is not a constructor function type.
    92 |  * It emits the 'render' event every time a search is done
    93 |  */
  > 94 | declare class InstantSearch<TUiState extends UiState = UiState, TRouteState = TUiState> extends EventEmitter {
       |                                                                                                 ^
    95 |     client: InstantSearchOptions['searchClient'];
    96 |     indexName: string;
    97 |     insightsClient: AlgoliaInsightsClient | null;
```

Both on Typescript 3.8.3 and 4.5.2 (this error message from 4.5.2). This also came up here: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/issues/4911 and required a different workaround. We're consuming this through vue-instantsearch.

I was just coming here to open this same PR to unblock our usage. Looks like we'll need to fork with this fix unless we can bring it in here.

Aaaand now when I try to build my fork I get the following build error: 

```
[!] Error: 'EventEmitter' is not exported by node_modules/events/events.js
https://rollupjs.org/guide/en/#error-name-is-not-exported-by-module
src/lib/InstantSearch.ts (3:9)
1: import type { AlgoliaSearchHelper } from 'algoliasearch-helper';
2: import algoliasearchHelper from 'algoliasearch-helper';
3: import { EventEmitter } from 'events';
            ^
4: import type { IndexWidget } from '../widgets/index/index';
5: import index, { isIndexWidget } from '../widgets/index/index';
Error: 'EventEmitter' is not exported by node_modules/events/events.js
    at error (/Users/jeff/workspace/instantsearch.js/node_modules/rollup/dist/rollup.js:5330:30)
    at Module.error (/Users/jeff/workspace/instantsearch.js/node_modules/rollup/dist/rollup.js:9733:16)
    at handleMissingExport (/Users/jeff/workspace/instantsearch.js/node_modules/rollup/dist/rollup.js:9634:28)
    at Module.traceVariable (/Users/jeff/workspace/instantsearch.js/node_modules/rollup/dist/rollup.js:10072:24)
    at ModuleScope.findVariable (/Users/jeff/workspace/instantsearch.js/node_modules/rollup/dist/rollup.js:8679:39)
    at Identifier$1.bind (/Users/jeff/workspace/instantsearch.js/node_modules/rollup/dist/rollup.js:4353:40)
    at CallExpression$1.bind (/Users/jeff/workspace/instantsearch.js/node_modules/rollup/dist/rollup.js:3098:31)
    at CallExpression$1.bind (/Users/jeff/workspace/instantsearch.js/node_modules/rollup/dist/rollup.js:6631:15)

```

Which is the same error referenced in https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/issues/2730. So indeed it looks like we have two competing environments that demand different import structures...

I upgraded node on my local machine from `v16.8.0` to `v17.0.1` and upgraded `@types/node` and it seemed to resolve the issue

@trestletech have you tried enabling `esModuleInterop: true` in your tsconfig? If that doesn't solve your issue, it'd be helpful to get a minimal example to help me reproduce, would you be able to provide that?
Fwiw I had similar issues with some Rollup configs.
Any chance this could be reopened? I'm getting the same. I can try and put together a minimal reproducible example if that helps?
@duhaime, does `esModuleInterop` and `allowSyntheticDefaultImports` not work for you? could you indeed create a reproducible example and a new issue please?

@Haroenv thanks for your fast follow up. Setting `esModuleInterop: true` resolves this error but opens up many other issues. I haven't been able to reproduce the problem in a minimal example yet, so I'm diving more deeply (I haven't worked with typescript in a few years). 

Hopefully I can get you something to work with soon. In my big baggy repo I get:

```
yarn run v1.22.17
$ tsc
pnode_modules/instantsearch.js/es/lib/InstantSearch.d.ts:94:97 - error TS2507: Type 'typeof EventEmitter' is not a constructor function type.

94 declare class InstantSearch<TUiState extends UiState = UiState, TRouteState = TUiState> extends EventEmitter {
                                                                                                   ~~~~~~~~~~~~
Found 1 error.

error Command failed with exit code 2.
```

In my environment, changing `import EventEmitter from 'events';` to `import { EventEmitter } from 'events'` resolves the issue. Can someone help me understand why `events` is showing unpredictable behavior here?

To resolve this error I just needed to install `@types/node` with a major version that matched my Node version. 

I.e. `node -v` returned `v14.18.1` so I added `"@types/node": "14.17.34",` (the last release of @types/node on major version 14) to my `packages.json` file and then `yarn` 🚀
This should be fixed more long-term by #4961, as it doesn't overlap with the node builtins
